summary: The appellant sought dissolution of marriage under Section 13(1)(ia) of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955, alleging cruelty due to strained relations between the respondent and the appellant's sister. The Family Court granted the decree, but the Madras High Court reversed it. The Supreme Court upheld the High Court's reversal, finding no evidence of matrimonial cruelty. The respondent had gone to her parental home during pregnancy and after her father's death, which did not amount to desertion or cruelty. The Court held that the marriage breakdown was not due to the respondent's fault and criticized the appellant's haste in remarrying without awaiting final appeal. It also examined the limitation period for appeal under Section 19 of the Family Courts Act and found the appeal was filed in time under Section 12 of the Limitation Act. The Court dismissed the appeal, affirming that the High Court correctly restored the marital tie.
final_judgment: Appeal dismissed; the impugned judgment of the High Court restoring the marital relationship is upheld.
